How the category looks and what it is called.

• Choose icon: the picture shown in lists, on the Add screen and in charts.
• Category name: the name shown everywhere the category appears.
• Color: tints its icon, progress bars and chart slices.

A monthly spending limit for this category. Spending in its sub-categories counts too. Each month has its own settings: pick the month next to the title, and your changes to each month are saved together when you tap Save. A later month with no settings of its own uses the last month before it; a change to a past month changes only that month. The switch turns the budget off for that month without losing its settings.

• Sum of subcategories (a parent category only): the limit is its subcategories' monthly limits that month added up, and follows them when they change. While on, the limit can't be typed and the over/under settings are hidden and not used; they are kept for when it is turned off.
• Monthly budget limit: how much you plan to spend that month.
• Over limit: take from: when a month goes over the limit, the overspend is taken off next month's limit of the budget you pick (this one or another).
• Under limit: add to: when a month ends under the limit, the unspent amount is added to next month's limit of the budget you pick. With Account, it is moved as real money instead: a transfer From one account To another, made the first time you open the app next month.

Spending in this sub-category is not counted in its parent category\'s budget, in every month (past months too). This sub-category\'s own budget still counts it, and the Analysis category charts are unchanged.

The account's basic details.

• Choose icon: the picture shown in lists and on trades.
• Normal / Savings: a savings account holds money set aside. Its balance is kept apart from the money you can spend, and it can have a monthly target.
• Account name: the name shown everywhere the account appears.
• Current balance: the money in the account now. Changing it records an adjustment for the difference, so your history stays correct.
• Color: tints its icon and chart lines.

A monthly goal for how much to put into this account. Only savings accounts can have one.

Each month has its own target: pick the month next to the title, and your changes to each month are saved together when you tap Save. A later month with no target of its own uses the last month before it; a change to a past month changes only that month.

• Monthly savings target: the amount to add that month. Income and transfers into the account count toward it.
• Sum of subaccounts (a parent account only): the target is its subaccounts' targets that month added up, and follows them when they change. While on, the target can't be typed; your own amount is kept for when it is turned off.

Money coming into this subaccount (income, and transfers from outside it) is not counted toward its parent account\'s monthly savings target, in every month (past months too). Balances still include it, and this subaccount\'s own savings target still counts it.

Choose what this account keeps out of sight. A parent account's settings also cover its subaccounts.

• Hide balance: the balance shows as •••••• on the Accounts screen. It is left out of Home's totals and out of Analysis' account charts.
• Hide savings progress (savings accounts only): Never; When reached, hidden once this month's target is met and shown again next month; or Always. A hidden progress has no row on Home and no bar on the Accounts screen.
• Show in Analysis: the progress stays hidden on Home and the Accounts screen but still shows in Analysis. A hidden balance stays hidden there.

Leave this trade out of every budget: its subcategory\'s own budget and its parent category\'s. It still counts in the Analysis category charts.\n\nIt can only be turned on when the trade\'s subcategory or its parent category has a budget, and it is always on for a subcategory marked Parent budget exception.

Leave this trade out of every savings target: the account\'s own monthly target and its parent account\'s. Balances still include it.\n\nOn an income it is the trade\'s account; on a transfer, the To account. It can only be turned on when that account is a savings account, and it is always on for a subaccount marked Parent saving exception.

How to read and use it
Tap a chart to add it. Press and hold to learn what it shows.
each account, with its subaccounts added up
the subaccounts of the account picked in the chip
each category, with its subcategories added up
the subcategories of the category picked in the chip
The balance at the end of every day of the month, one line for %1$s.
Shows when money came in and went out, and how each balance moved through the month. Accounts with a hidden balance are left out.
Slide a finger sideways to read a day\'s balance. Tap a line or its name to pick it out. Use the chips to hide accounts or make the axis start at 0.
The month-end balance of %1$s as a pie, each with its change since the month before.
Shows where your money sits and which balances grew or shrank. A balance at or below 0 gets no slice.
Tap a slice or a row to pick it out; the list scrolls to it. Use the chip to hide accounts.
The month-end balance of %1$s over the last 5 months, stacked into one bar per month.
Shows whether your money is growing, and how much of it each account holds. Negative balances stack below 0.
Slide a finger across the bars to read a month\'s total. Use the chip to hide accounts.
Your %1$s for %2$s, added up from the 1st of the month: each line climbs with every day that has money.
Steep stretches are days with a lot of %1$s, flat ones are quiet days. The last point of a line is that category\'s total so far. Only categories with money this month show.
Slide a finger sideways to read a day\'s total. Tap a line or its name to pick it out. Use the chips to hide categories or make the axis start at 0.
This month\'s %1$s split across %2$s as a pie, each with its change since last month.
Shows which categories take the biggest share of your %1$s, and which grew or shrank since last month.
Tap a slice or a row to pick it out; the list scrolls to it. Use the chip to hide categories.
Your %1$s for %2$s over the last 5 months, stacked into one bar per month.
Shows the trend of your %1$s and how its mix of categories changes from month to month.
Slide a finger across the bars to read a month\'s total. Use the chip to hide categories.
The month in numbers: the total of the kind picked in the chip, its change since last month, the average per day and the money moved between your accounts.

With All, the total is income minus expense: what the month left you. On the current month the daily average divides by the days so far. Transfers move money between your own accounts, so they are not counted as spending or income.
Pick Expense, Income or All in the chip. Green is good for you and red is not: spending more than last month shows red, earning more shows green.
The month as a calendar, each day shaded by how much money moved that day.

Darker days are heavier days. With Expense it shows spending in red, with Income earnings in green, and with All the day\'s net: green when more came in than went out, red otherwise. Spotting the heavy days helps you see what drives your month.
Tap a day to see its total and number of trades, then tap Open to list that day\'s trades in History. The line under the calendar names the busiest day. Pick the kind in the chip.
The month\'s trades by day of the week (rows) and four-hour slot of the day (columns).
Darker cells are the times you spend (or earn) the most, so habits like weekend evenings or lunch breaks stand out. With All, expenses and income add up.
Tap a cell to see its amount and number of trades. Trades are placed by the time saved on them. Pick the kind in the chip.
The month\'s trades grouped by size. Each group has two bars: its share of the number of trades and its share of the money.
Tells you whether many small trades or a few large ones make up your money. A tall trades bar with a short money bar means frequent but cheap; the other way round means rare but big.
Slide a finger across the bars to read a group\'s trade count and amount. A group is labelled with where it starts: 100K+ runs from 100K up to the next group. Pick the kind in the chip.
The 10 largest trades of the month, largest first.
These single trades weigh most on your month: the first place to look when a month went over.
Scroll the list inside the card. Tap a trade to open it for editing. The faint bar behind each row is its size next to the largest. Pick the kind in the chip.
The last 6 months: bars count the trades, the line is the average amount per trade.
Separates spending more often from spending on dearer things: taller bars with a flat line mean more trades, a rising line means bigger ones.
Slide a finger across to read a month\'s count and average. Pick the kind in the chip.
This month\'s transfers between your accounts: senders on the left, receivers on the right.
Each band is as thick as the money it carries, so you see where money is moved from and where it ends up. Beyond the largest few, the remaining accounts join Other.
Read each account\'s total beside it. The line at the bottom gives the number of transfers and their total.
Every savings account with a target this month: what you have saved so far against the target.

The solid tick is the target. The dashed tick is where you would be today saving at an even pace. The faint bar is where the month ends if you keep your pace so far. The caption says whether you are ahead or behind.

Only money that counts toward the target is included: income into the account and transfers in from other accounts. An account whose progress is hidden stays out unless you keep it in Analysis. Scroll inside the card for more accounts.
One savings account\'s month: the amount saved, added up day by day.
The grey dashed line climbs evenly from 0 to the target; above it you are ahead. The dashed line from today shows where the month ends at your pace so far.
Pick the account in the chip. Slide a finger sideways to read a day; tap a line or its name to pick it out.
Each savings account\'s target over the last 12 months, one cell per month.
A full green cell is a month the target was hit; lighter cells show how close you got; grey means no target that month. Streak counts the months in a row the target was hit, up to now.
Tap a cell to see the amount saved and the target that month. The current month doesn\'t break a streak until it is over.
The last 6 months: bars are the money saved into your savings accounts, the line is that amount as a share of the month\'s income.
The share tells you how much of what you earn you keep. A steady or rising line is a healthy habit.
Slide a finger across to read a month\'s amount saved, income and share. Accounts whose progress is hidden are left out.
One savings account\'s balance from the start of the month to its end, step by step.
Green steps add money: income, transfers in, budget leftovers moved in automatically, and money that doesn\'t count toward the target. Red steps take it away: spending and transfers out.
Pick the account in the chip and read each step\'s amount on the right. Accounts with a hidden balance are not offered.
Every budget this month: spent so far against its limit, the riskiest first.

The solid tick is the limit after carry-over and top-ups. The dashed tick is where spending would be today at an even pace. The faint bar is where the month ends if you keep spending at your pace so far. Red: over. Yellow: heading over. Green: on track.

Scroll inside the card for more budgets. On a past month the bars show the final result. The forecast assumes the same spending every day, so a large bill paid early in the month makes it look worse than it is.
One budget\'s month: what is left of it at the end of each day.

Below the grey dashed line you are spending faster than an even pace; below 0 the budget is overspent. Top-ups show as steps up. The dashed line from today shows where the month ends at your pace so far.
Pick the budget in the chip. Slide a finger sideways to read a day; tap a line or its name to pick it out.
Every budget over the last 6 months, with the share of its limit used each month.
Green is comfortably under the limit, yellow is close to it (over 80%), red is over it. Over counts the months above the limit. Grey means the budget was off that month.
Tap a cell to see what was spent and the limit that month. Scroll inside the card for more budgets.
How one budget\'s limit this month comes about, and what is left of it.

It starts from the limit you set (or its subcategories\' limits added up), adds what was carried over from last month and any top-ups, then takes away what was spent. A red Left means the budget is overspent.
Pick the budget in the chip and read each step\'s amount on the right.
Your spending over the last 6 months, split into spending in a category with a budget, spending with no budget, and spending left out of budgets.
The more of each bar is in a budget, the more of your spending your budgets keep an eye on. The line below gives this month\'s share.
Slide a finger across the bars to read a month\'s total. Left out is spending marked as a budget exception.
For each budget, the day of the month it went over its limit, in each of the last 6 months.
Dots far to the left mean the money runs out early in the month. The newest month is the large, ringed dot; older months are paler. Avg is the usual day; a dash means it never went over.
Scroll inside the card for more budgets. A month the budget was off or stayed under its limit has no dot.
